metadata.dataset_name: Grade Control and Reconciliation Knowledge Base
metadata.description: Comprehensive grade control, sampling, estimation, reconciliation, and quality assurance dataset for mineral resource operations

grid_patterns.notes: Pattern selection depends on geological complexity, nugget effect, and commodity type. High-nugget deposits (Au) require tighter spacing. Base metal deposits may tolerate wider spacing due to larger mineralised envelopes.

definition.drill_consumables: Diamond core bits (surface set or impregnated)

chip_sampling.description: Systematic collection of rock chips from blast hole cuttings or face mappings
chip_sampling.collection_method: Continuous riffle or grid-based chip collection from blow cuttings at regular intervals during drilling
chip_sampling.interval: Every 1 to 2 metres or every 3 to 5 metres of face advance
advantages: Large sample volume improves representivity for nuggety ores
Can be collected during normal production drilling
disadvantages: Potential for preferential sampling of harder lithologies
quality_measures: Calibrated chip trays for consistent interval lengths
GPS coordinates of sample collection points
Sterilisation of collection tools between samples

rinse_sampling.description: Collection of fine fraction from drill water circulation during blast hole drilling
rinse_sampling.collection_method: Filtered from drilling return water using settling tanks or fine mesh screens
advantages: Captures fine fraction that may be lost in chip sampling
Rapid method for near-surface weathered material
Good for alluvial or saprolitic material
disadvantages: Not suitable for hard rock fresh material
quality_measures: Standardised mesh size for all holes
Consistent settling time of 30 minutes minimum

auger_sampling.description: Hand-operated or machine auger collection from soft or weathered material in blast holes
auger_sampling.collection_method: Continuous or interval sampling using hand auger or machine-mounted auger with core barrel
advantages: Provides continuous sample through soft zones
quality_measures: Interval bags clearly labelled with hole ID, depth, and date
Storage in cool dry conditions before dispatch

channel_sampling.description: Continuous channels cut perpendicular to geological features using chisel or diamond saw
channel_sampling.collection_method: Dust-free diamond saw cutting with vacuum extraction, or pneumatic chisel
advantages: Industry standard for underground grade control
quality_measures: Constant channel width maintained with guides
No preferential following of mineralised zones

fire_assay.flux_composition: Litharge (PbO), soda ash (Na2CO3), borax (Na2B4O7), flour (C source), silica (SiO2)
fire_assay.description: Lead collection fire assay followed by gravimetric or AAS finish. Industry standard for precious metals. Inquart technique used when Cu or Ni exceeds 2%.
advantages: Most accurate method for precious metals
Large sample mass (25-50g) improves representivity for nuggety ores
Widely accepted by all major reporting codes

AAS.sample_preparation: Acid digestion (HNO3, HCl, HF, HClO4) or fusion with lithium metaborate
AAS.description: Element-specific absorption of light by ground-state atoms in a flame or graphite furnace. Flame AAS is the workhorse for base metals in grade control laboratories.
disadvantages: Sequential analysis (one element at a time)
Limited dynamic range compared to ICP

ICP_MS.description: Multi-element analysis using argon plasma to ionise atoms followed by mass-to-charge separation. Provides full geochemical suite in a single run.
advantages: Wide dynamic range (9 orders of magnitude)

XRF.sample_preparation: Pressed pellets or fused glass beads for WDXRF; surface preparation for handheld
XRF.description: Non-destructive technique measuring secondary X-rays emitted when sample is irradiated. Handheld units used for rapid field screening. WDXRF used in laboratory for major and minor elements.
disadvantages: Cannot detect light elements (H, C, N, O, Li)
Lower precision than wet chemistry for trace elements

LECO_combustion.method: Infrared detection of CO2 and SO2 after combustion in pure O2
LECO_combustion.description: High-frequency induction furnace combustion with infrared cell detection for total carbon and sulfur. Used for refractory gold ores (carbonaceous material) and sulfide deportment studies.
disadvantages: Cannot distinguish organic from inorganic carbon without additional thermal treatment

drying.equipment: Industrial tray dryers or rotary dish dryers
drying.notes: Samples must be oven-dried to constant weight. Temperature must not exceed 110°C to avoid mineral alteration. Air drying acceptable for non-hygroscopic samples.

crushing.cleaning_protocol: Crush barren quartz or sample from previous batch between each sample to prevent cross-contamination

pulverising.equipment: Ring mill (stainless steel or tungsten carbide ring and puck)
pulverising.description: Sample is pulverised to P80 of 75 microns (200 mesh) for assay. Ring mill preferred for base metals; ceramic or agate mills for trace element work.
quality_checks: Sieve analysis at 1:50 ratio to verify grind size
Ring and puck inspection for wear
Sound monitoring for correct charge weight

sub_sampling.method: Riffle splitting or cone and quartering
sub_sampling.description: Representative sub-sample obtained by mechanical splitting. Minimum 3 stages of splitting recommended to achieve assay charge from 1kg pulp.

standards.control_chart_method: Shewhart charts with Western Electric rules
standards.notes: Standards must be from different supplier or batch than previous quarter to avoid laboratory bias. At least 3 different CRMs used per quarter.

types.inprocedural_blank: Pulverised barren quartz inserted into sample preparation stream
types.field_blank: Barren material carried to field and processed through entire workflow

blanks.notes: Blanks monitor contamination in sample preparation and analysis. Elevated blank results trigger investigation and potential re-preparation of affected batch.

types.field_duplicate: Second sample collected from same blast hole at same interval
types.prep_duplicate: Second split of same prepared pulp sent for analysis
types.coarse_duplicate: Second split of crushed material before pulverising

acceptance_criteria.relative_difference_pct: 15 for Au, 20 for base metals at 95% confidence

duplicates.precision_assessment: Comparing difference between duplicates against expected analytical precision

control_charts.description: Individual measurement chart with mean and control limits at 1, 2, and 3 standard deviations
rules: 8 consecutive points on one side of mean = shift

control_charts.description: Accumulates deviations from target value to detect small sustained shifts
control_charts.advantage: More sensitive than Shewhart for detecting small persistent changes

control_charts.description: Gives decreasing weight to older observations using exponential smoothing
control_charts.advantage: Effective for detecting small shifts while retaining information from recent data

control_charts.description: Graphical comparison of results from two independent laboratories or methods
control_charts.criteria: Points should cluster around the 45-degree line if no bias exists

control_charts.description: Plots coefficient of variation against grade to assess precision across the grade range

ordinary_kriging.description: Best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) that uses weighted average of nearby samples with weights derived from variogram model. Assumes constant but unknown mean within the search neighbourhood.
ordinary_kriging.mathematical_basis: Minimises estimation variance E{[Z*(x) - Z(x)]^2} subject to constraint that weights sum to 1
advantages: Provides estimation variance (kriging variance) as measure of confidence
Accounts for spatial correlation via variogram
disadvantages: May oversmooth extreme values (high grade or low grade)
Can produce negative estimates for bounded variables
May not honour data exactly (not an exact interpolator at data points if neighbourhood is restricted)

parameters.variogram_model: Spherical, exponential, or Gaussian model fitted to experimental variogram

search_ellipsoid.semi_axes: Defined by variogram range in major, minor, and vertical directions
search_ellipsoid.sectorisation: Typically 2 to 4 sectors to ensure directional coverage

parameters.discretisation: 3x3x3 or 5x5x5 points within each block for numerical integration

inverse_distance_weighting.description: Deterministic interpolation where weights are inversely proportional to distance raised to a power. Simple to implement but lacks statistical framework.
inverse_distance_weighting.formula: Z*(x) = Σ(wi * Zi) / Σ(wi), where wi = 1/di^p
advantages: Can be applied directly in most software
disadvantages: Results depend on arbitrary power selection
Cannot account for anisotropy without modification
Tends to create bull's-eye patterns around data points

nearest_neighbour.description: Assigns the value of the closest sample to each block centre. Non-averaging method that preserves grade variability.
advantages: Preserves grade variability and grade tonnage curves
Useful for comparisons with other methods
disadvantages: No smoothing effect may overestimate selectivity
Does not use information from multiple samples
use_cases: Comparison benchmark for other estimation methods
Highly variable deposits with strong nugget effect
Quick grade model for preliminary pit design

multiple_indicator_kriging.description: Non-parametric geostatistical method that estimates the proportion of blocks above a series of grade thresholds using indicator variables and indicator variograms.
advantages: Does not assume a specific distribution
Useful for deposits with mixed populations
disadvantages: Requires multiple variogram models (one per threshold)
Less commonly available in commercial software
use_cases: When conditional simulation is not feasible

discrete_kriging.description: Variation of MIK that uses a smaller number of thresholds and applies rank-order statistics to build local histograms.

ordinary_cokriging.description: Extension of ordinary kriging that uses spatial correlation between a primary variable (hard to measure) and secondary variables (easier to measure, better sampled).
advantages: Uses information from correlated secondary variables
Improves estimates where primary data is sparse
disadvantages: Requires co-located samples of both variables
use_cases: Au estimation using As or pathfinder geochemistry
Using grade control data to improve resource model

types.name: Spherical
types.equation: γ(h) = C₀ + C × [1.5(h/a) - 0.5(h/a)³] for h ≤ a; γ(h) = C₀ + C for h > a
types.description: Most commonly used model. Reaches sill at finite range a. Has linear behaviour near origin.
types.applicability: Default model for most mineral deposits

types.name: Exponential
types.description: Approaches sill asymptotically. Practical range (95% of sill) used as effective range. Steeper near origin than spherical.

types.name: Gaussian
types.description: Parabolic behaviour near origin indicating very smooth grade variation. Practical range at 95% of sill.
types.applicability: Smoothly varying deposits (e.g., coal, some base metals)

types.name: Linear
types.description: No sill reached within the data support. Indicates non-stationary or trend behaviour.

types.name: Power
types.equation: γ(h) = C₀ + C × h^w where 0 < w < 2
types.description: No sill. Exponent w controls curvature. w=1 is linear model.

types.name: Nugget
types.equation: γ(h) = C₀ if h > 0; γ(h) = 0 if h = 0
types.description: Pure nugget effect with no spatial continuity. Represents random variability at the sample support.
types.applicability: Highly irregular deposits, sampling error assessment

nugget.description: Micro-scale variability and/or measurement error. Represents discontinuity at the origin of the variogram.
nugget.interpretation: High nugget (>50% of sill) indicates poor spatial continuity and limits estimation accuracy

sill.description: Variance level at which variogram levels off. Should approximate sample variance for stationary data.
sill.interpretation: Total variance of the data. If experimental variogram exceeds sill, indicates non-stationarity.
sill.estimation: Calculated from sample variance or estimated from variogram plateau

range.description: Distance at which variogram reaches the sill. Beyond this distance, samples are uncorrelated.
range.interpretation: Defines the search radius for kriging. Samples beyond range are statistically independent.

anisotropy.description: Variation of variogram parameters with direction. Geometric anisotropy varies range; zonal anisotropy varies sill.

major_axis.determination: From geological trend, structural data, or variogram surface plotting

minor_axis.description: Direction of minimum horizontal spatial continuity, perpendicular to major axis
minor_axis.determination: Perpendicular to major axis in horizontal plane

vertical_axis.description: Direction of continuity in the vertical dimension
vertical_axis.determination: From vertical variograms on drill hole data
vertical_axis.typical_values: Usually shorter range than horizontal due to geological layering

experimental_variogram.lag_distance: Set at average sample spacing or multiple thereof
experimental_variogram.number_of_pairs: Minimum 30 pairs per lag for reliable estimate
experimental_variogram.bandwidth: Half-width of search cylinder perpendicular to lag direction
experimental_variogram.outlier_handling: Samples contributing to extreme semi-variance values flagged and investigated

cross_validation.method: Leave-one-out cross validation where each sample is estimated from remaining samples
metrics: Mean Standardised Error (MSE) should be close to 0
Root Mean Square Standardised Error (RMSSE) should be close to 1
Correlation between estimated and actual values
cross_validation.acceptance_criteria: RMSSE between 0.9 and 1.1 indicates appropriate variogram model and search parameters

block_model_parameters.coordinate_system: Local mine grid or national grid (UTM)

compositing.length_preference: Equal to or integer multiple of block model bench height
compositing.top_composite_handling: Short composites merged with adjacent if > 50% of nominal length; otherwise discarded
compositing.sliver_handling: Composites < 50% of nominal length discarded or merged with adjacent

level_0_operational.name: Operational Reconciliation
level_0_operational.description: Daily reconciliation of blast hole sampling results against grade control model predictions for each blast pattern
level_0_operational.compares: Blast hole assay results vs predicted grade from grade control model
level_0_operational.purpose: Immediate feedback on model accuracy and blast design

level_1_mine_to_mill.name: Level 1: Mine to Mill
level_1_mine_to_mill.description: Comparing grade control model predictions to actual plant head grade after processing
level_1_mine_to_mill.compares: Grade control model grade and tonnage vs plant head grade from sampling or mass balance
level_1_mine_to_mill.purpose: Assess accuracy of grade control model in predicting what enters the processing plant
key_challenges: Blend of material from multiple blocks
Sampling differences between grade control and plant
Time lag between mining and processing

level_2_mill_to_refinery.name: Level 2: Mill to Refinery
level_2_mill_to_refinery.description: Comparing concentrate grade and recovery from the processing plant to refined metal produced at the smelter/refinery
level_2_mill_to_refinery.compares: Plant concentrate production (grade, recovery) vs smelter/refinery metal production
level_2_mill_to_refinery.purpose: Assess metallurgical recovery accuracy and smelter treatment

level_3_reserve_to_actual.name: Level 3: Reserve to Actual Production
level_3_reserve_to_actual.description: Comparing the original resource/reserve model estimates to total actual production over the life of mine
level_3_reserve_to_actual.compares: Resource model and reserve estimate vs cumulative actual production
level_3_reserve_to_actual.purpose: Evaluate the overall accuracy and reliability of the resource model

level_4_model_validation.name: Level 4: Model Validation
level_4_model_validation.description: Comparison of original geological model against all available data including production data, to validate or refine the model
level_4_model_validation.compares: Original resource model vs updated model incorporating production data
level_4_model_validation.purpose: Continuous improvement of geological understanding and model accuracy

metal_reconciliation.formula: Actual metal contained / Planned metal contained × 100

dilution_factor.formula: Total tonnes mined / Ore tonnes mined

mining_loss.formula: (Planned ore tonnes - Actual ore tonnes) / Planned ore tonnes × 100

causes: Variability in geological interpretation between resource model and grade control
Unidentified fault displacement affecting ore continuity
Changes in alteration style or intensity not captured in model
Inclusion of waste in ore domains or exclusion of ore from domains
Nugget effect causing grade variability beyond model resolution
Mixed geological populations within estimation domains
Variation in mineralogy affecting metallurgical recovery
Differences in sample support (blast hole vs RC vs diamond core)
Sample preparation errors (crushing, pulverising, splitting)
Analytical bias between laboratories
Selective sampling of specific lithologies
Sample contamination in the field or laboratory
Incorrect sample compositing lengths
Representativeness issues with chip samples in nuggety ore
Dilution from blast hole deviation
Overbreak or underbreak of stope walls
Incorrect blast design causing ore/waste mixing
Selective mining not matching grade control boundaries
Stockpile management and re-handling effects
Grade control model not updated in time for mining
Bench floor irregularities causing ore loss
Fogging or smearing at ore/waste contacts
Plant feed blend differing from planned sequence
Metallurgical recovery variations due to ore type changes
Process plant upsets or maintenance downtime
Changes in reagent suite or operating parameters
Particle size distribution variations in mill feed
Moisture content differences affecting head grade calculation
Small number of samples in reconciliation period
Extreme values (outliers) distorting averages
Different averaging methods (arithmetic vs weighted)
Volume-variance effects between sample and block supports
Change of support correction not applied
Regression effects in grade estimation

reconciliation_workflow.daily: Grade control data updated, blast pattern reconciliation initiated
reconciliation_workflow.weekly: Blast-by-blast reconciliation report, grade control model updates
reconciliation_workflow.monthly: Full Level 1 reconciliation with plant data, stockpile reconciliation
reconciliation_workflow.quarterly: Level 2 reconciliation, resource model review, variogram updates
reconciliation_workflow.annually: Level 3 and Level 4 reconciliation, reserve statement update
reconciliation_workflow.life_of_mine: Complete reconciliation study, model validation report

geological_logging.code_of_practice: Geological logging must follow the site Geological Standard Operating Procedure (GSOP) which defines coding schemes, logging intervals, and description requirements. Logging should be performed by qualified geologists with a minimum of 2 years site experience.
parameters: Geotechnical features (RQD, fracture frequency, joint sets)

logging_standards.descriptions: Free text with minimum 50 words per metre for significant zones
logging_standards.quality_audit: Monthly peer review of logging accuracy

chain_of_custody.description: Documented trail from sample collection through preparation and analysis to final result
documentation: Sample collection forms (GPS coordinates, date, collector, interval)
Sample bags with unique tamper-evident tags
chain_of_custody.retention_period: Minimum 5 years from date of collection
chain_of_custody.digital_tracking: Barcode or QR code system with database backend

rules: Never reused even after hole abandonment
Year component prevents ambiguity across decades

sample_storage.pulp_storage: Retained in labelled containers in climate-controlled facility

ISO_17025.full_name: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 - General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories
ISO_17025.relevance: International standard for laboratory accreditation ensuring technical competence and quality management
key_requirements: Competent technical staff with demonstrated qualifications

NADCAP.full_name: National Aerospace and Defense Contractors Accreditation Program
NADCAP.relevance: Specialised accreditation for specific testing disciplines, often required by major mining companies

providers: ASCTS (Australasian Society for Coal Sample Testing)
proficiency_testing.action_on_failure: Investigation within 5 working days, corrective action within 20 working days

requirements: Limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantitation (LOQ) established
Accuracy verified against certified reference materials

data_management.data_validation: Automated range checks, geological consistency checks, duplicate analysis
data_management.audit_trail: All data modifications logged with user, timestamp, and reason

JORC_2012.full_name: Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves (JORC Code 2012)
JORC_2012.governing_body: Joint Ore Reserves Committee (JORC) of the Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, Australian Institute of Geoscientists, and Minerals Council of Australia

key_definitions.Exploration_Results: Data and information produced by exploration which may be used to indicate the existence of a mineral resource or ore reserve
key_definitions.Mineral_Resource: A concentration or occurrence of material of economic interest in or on the Earth's crust in such form, grade or quality and quantity that there are reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction
key_definitions.Ore_Reserve: The economically mineable part of a Measured and/or Indicated Mineral Resource
key_definitions.Modifying_Factors: Considerations used to convert Mineral Resources to Ore Reserves including mining, metallurgical, economic, marketing, legal, environmental, social and government factors

resource_categories.Inferred: Quantity and grade estimated on the basis of limited geological evidence and sampling. Low confidence.
resource_categories.Indicated: Quantity, grade or quality estimated with sufficient confidence to allow Mine Planning and evaluation of economic viability.
resource_categories.Measured: Quantity, grade or quality estimated with confidence sufficient to allow Mine Planning and evaluation of economic viability.

competent_person.requirements: A minerals industry Competent Person must be a Fellow or Member of the Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy or Australian Institute of Geoscientists
competent_person.experience: Minimum 5 years experience in the style of mineralisation or deposit type under consideration
competent_person.responsibility: Personally responsible for the information in the public report

reporting_requirements: Clear statement of assumptions and criteria
Tonnage and grade at specified cut-off grades
Quality assurance and quality control information

NI_43_101.full_name: National Instrument 43-101: Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects
applicable_jurisdictions: International operations listed on Canadian exchanges

key_definitions.Technical_Report: A report prepared under NI 43-101 by a Qualified Person that provides detailed scientific and technical information about a mineral project
key_definitions.Mineral_Resource: A concentration or occurrence of diamonds, natural solid inorganic material, or natural solid fossilized organic material in or on the Earth's crust in such form and grade and in such quantity that there are reasonable prospects for the eventual economic extraction of the mineral or minerals
key_definitions.Mineral_Reserve: The economically mineable portion of a Measured and/or Indicated Mineral Resource

qualified_person.requirements: An engineer or geoscientist with at least 5 years of experience in mineral exploration, mine development or mine operations, relevant to the style of mineralization
qualified_person.accreditation: Must be a member in good standing of a professional organization in a Canadian province or territory
qualified_person.responsibility: Responsible for the preparation or supervision of the preparation of the technical report

reporting_categories.Inferred: That part of a Mineral Resource for which quantity and grade or quality can be estimated on the basis of geological evidence and limited sampling
reporting_categories.Indicated: That part of a Mineral Resource for which quantity, grade or quality, are estimated or can be inferred with a level of confidence sufficient to allow Mine Planning
reporting_categories.Measured: That part of a Mineral Resource for which quantity, grade or quality, are estimated or can be inferred with a high level of confidence

technical_report_triggers: Filing of a prospectus or similar offering document
Material change in Mineral Resource or Mineral Reserve estimates
Material adverse change in mineral properties
reporting_requirements: Accessibility, climate, local resources and infrastructure

SAMREC.full_name: South African Code for Reporting of Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves (The SAMREC Code)
SAMREC.governing_body: South African Mineral Resources Committee (SAMREC) of the Chamber of Mines of South Africa

key_definitions.Mineral_Resource: A concentration or occurrence of material of economic interest in or on the Earth's crust in such form, grade or quality and quantity that there are reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction
key_definitions.Ore_Reserve: The economically mineable part of a Measured and/or Indicated Mineral Resource, including diluting materials and allowances for losses, which may occur when the material is mined

competent_person.requirements: Must be registered with a recognised professional body (ECSA, SACNASP, or equivalent)
competent_person.registration: Must hold Pr.Eng, Pr.Sci.Nat, Pr.Sci.Min, or equivalent

resource_categories.Inferred: Estimate based on limited geological evidence and sampling
resource_categories.Indicated: Estimate based on detailed sampling and testing sufficient for Mine Planning
resource_categories.Measured: Estimate based on detailed sampling and testing with high confidence

AUSIMM_code.full_name: AusIMM Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves (2014)
AUSIMM_code.governing_body: Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy (AusIMM)
AUSIMM_code.note: The AusIMM Code is aligned with the JORC Code and provides additional guidance specific to AusIMM members

CIM.full_name: Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum (CIM) Definition Standards

UNFC.full_name: United Nations Framework Classification for Resources
UNFC.note: International classification system for energy and mineral resources

PERC.full_name: Pan-European Reserves and Resources Reporting Committee
PERC.note: European reporting standard aligned with JORC and CRIRSCO

CRIRSCO.full_name: Committee for Mineral Reserves International Reporting Standards
CRIRSCO.note: International template for mineral resource and reserve reporting codes

planning: Establish grade control philosophy document before mining commences
Define cut-off grades based on economic analysis including mining, processing, and refining costs
Set up sampling grid patterns appropriate for geological complexity
Establish QA/QC protocols before production drilling begins
Train all personnel in grade control procedures
execution: Update grade control model after every 5 to 10 blast patterns
Maintain minimum 2-week advance of grade control ahead of mining
Blend high-grade and low-grade material to maintain consistent mill feed
Track grade control predictions against actual mining results
Investigate all significant reconciliation variances immediately
reporting: Generate daily grade control reports for mining team
Monthly comprehensive grade control and reconciliation report
Quarterly resource model review and update
Annual reserve statement and life-of-mine reconciliation
continuous_improvement: Benchmark grade control performance against industry standards
Conduct annual review of sampling methods and equipment
Implement new technologies (XRF, hyperspectral, AI) as they become available
Document lessons learned and best practices

break_even.formula: COG = (Mining cost + Processing cost + G&A) / (Metal price × Recovery - Refining cost)
break_even.description: Grade at which revenue equals total cost. No profit or loss.

marginal.formula: COG = Marginal mining cost / (Metal price × Recovery - Processing cost - Refining cost)
marginal.description: Grade above which incremental tonnes contribute positive value

optimal.description: Maximises NPV by considering mining, processing, and refining capacity constraints

sensitivity_analysis.reporting: Spider diagrams, tornado charts, sensitivity tables
sensitivity_analysis.acceptable_ranges: NPV remains positive across reasonable sensitivity range

nugget_effect_management.description: High-nugget effect deposits (typically Au, Sn, W) present significant grade control challenges due to extreme short-range variability
strategies: High-density diamond drilling for grade control
Bulk sampling programs to validate grade control predictions
Use of nearest neighbour estimation to preserve variability
Conditional simulation to assess grade uncertainty
Blending strategies to reduce mill feed variability
Geometallurgical approaches to understand recovery variability
Coggan variogram analysis with multiple data supports
statistical_measures: Coefficient of variation (CV) > 100% indicates high nugget effect
Nugget-to-sill ratio > 50% suggests significant short-range variability
Histogram analysis for bi-modal or multi-modal distributions

geometallurgy.description: Integration of geometrical, mineralogical, and metallurgical data into the resource model to predict processing behaviour and recovery
block_model_integration: Assign geometallurgical domains to each block
Predict recovery at the block level
Use recovery-adjusted block values for mine planning
Update metallurgical model with production data

oxide_ore.recovery_impact: Higher recovery in some processes, lower in others

mixed_ore.recovery_impact: Variable, requires blending or selective processing
